Sources beside the text.

The manuscripts, historical references and earlier work that guided our research.

  1. Marie de’ Medici to Brèves, 15 September 1610

    BnF, Manuscripts department, Français 3789, f. 17r. Local image supplied by Brice, Gallica frame 32.

  2. Marie de’ Medici to Brèves, 10 November 1610

    BnF, Manuscripts department, Français 3789, f. 19r. Local image supplied by Brice, Gallica frame 36.

    View on Gallica ↗

  3. Key used for the comparisons

    BnF, Français 3462, frame 112. Satoshi confirms this key image for Henri IV–Brèves. Its exact application to Marie’s letters remains to be checked.

    View the key on Gallica ↗

  4. The 1610 succession and regency

    Château de Versailles, “Louis XIII”. Background on Henri IV’s death, Louis XIII’s accession and Marie de’ Medici’s regency. Consulted 16 October 2026; used for context, not to establish the cipher.

    Read the entry ↗

  5. Savoy and the Bruzolo agreements

    Les États de Savoie (1416–1861), Classiques Garnier, 2019, p. 233 onwards. University of Turin IRIS excerpt.

    Read the excerpt ↗

  6. Catalogue description of Français 3789

    BnF description reproduced by Biblissima: Marie’s letters of 15 September and 10 November 1610 are items 11 and 12. Used to check identification and the collection’s setting.

    Read the catalogue ↗

  7. Satoshi Tomokiyo — Cryptiana

    Satoshi Tomokiyo’s pages on the ciphers of Henri IV and Louis XIII helped identify Marie de’ Medici’s two letters and directed the search towards Brèves’s ciphers and Français 3462. Earlier work on Henri IV’s letter of 5 January 1610 is distinct from this decipherment of Marie’s letters.

    Cryptiana — Regent Marie de Medici ↗
    Cryptiana — Ciphers of Henry IV ↗

    Feedback from Satoshi Tomokiyo supplied on 17 October 2026. He confirms the Français 3462 image and the mistyped “3642” shelfmark, and supplies matching values for QUE, RE, SE and TION. This contribution supports six numerical occurrences; it does not validate the whole reading of Marie’s passages.

  8. Daniel Bourdeau — catalogue and comparative transcription

    Entry 25 in Daniel Bourdeau’s catalogue helped locate the dossier. His transcription of both passages also served as a comparison for our initial reading of the signs. We cite those documentary contributions; his earlier attempt had not yielded the passages’ plaintext.

    Read the catalogue ↗

Earlier work and this first decipherment

The research dossier follows leads recorded by S. Tomokiyo, Klaus Schmeh and Daniel Bourdeau. It also mentions earlier work by George Lasry, Norbert Biermann and S. Tomokiyo on a letter from Henri IV to Brèves, relevant to identifying the key. This site does not claim their work as its own.

To our knowledge, this site presents a first decipherment of Marie de’ Medici’s two passages. Daniel Bourdeau’s catalogue, checked on 16 October 2026, still lists the 10 November letter as “attempted, open”, with its 15 September sibling. Cryptiana also lists them as undeciphered in the consulted references. This statement concerns Marie’s letters, distinct from Henri IV’s letter studied by Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo. Some characters remain probable but unconfirmed.

Credits and reuse

The editorial model and visual principles follow Wenmi, by Brice Dudout with Claude: paper background, reading typography, history, method and inspectable documents. This implementation has its own files and does not modify Wenmi.

Original edition text and code: CC BY 4.0. Facsimiles are from BnF / Gallica and retain their separate reuse conditions; the site licence does not replace them. No archive image was generated by AI.

Two atmosphere illustrations were generated with imagegen: a writing desk and a courier towards Rome. Their captions identify them; they are not historical evidence. The manuscript-letter logo is a vector drawing made for this site.
